claims.text: In AlxCoCrFeNi alloys, toughness retention or loss is governed by precipitate formation and morphology.
Optimally sized coherent or semi-coherent precipitates act as crack-deflection sites.
Crack deflection by coherent or semi-coherent precipitates retains or improves toughness.
Overgrown or incoherent precipitates act as stress concentrators that initiate cracks and reduce toughness.
Solution treatment of AlxCoCrFeNi at 1200°C produces a fully single-phase state.
The solution-treated AlxCoCrFeNi baseline contains no pre-existing precipitates.
Aging between 600°C and 800°C for 2–8 hours can induce precipitate formation.
Holding atmosphere and cooling rate constant isolates aging temperature and time as the controlled processing variables.
Precipitate size, distribution, and coherency can be characterized using TEM.
Coherent or semi-coherent precipitates dissipate energy during fracture.
Loss of precipitate coherency during over-aging promotes crack propagation.
An optimal aging window will produce statistically higher fracture toughness than the single-phase baseline.
Aging conditions that produce coarse or incoherent precipitates will cause a measurable toughness decrease.
The proposed behavior applies within 600°C–800°C and aging times of 2–8 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Below or otherwise outside the stated processing window, too little precipitation may occur.
Outside the stated processing window, over-aging may dominate.
A lack of correlation between fine coherent precipitates and increased toughness, or toughness changes without corresponding precipitate changes, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
